name: Hitnu
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Lobo-Guerrero, Miguel 1979. El macaguane y la familia linguistica guahibo. Bogota: Universidad Nacional de Colombia. 137pp grammar sketch (Glottolog ref 92985); no online copy found

new_statements.quote: La palabra fonológica o grupo acentual en macaguán puede estar constituido de dos a cinco sílabas. La sílaba nuclear lleva un acento fonológico, con tono ligeramente alto, así como una ligera duración del sonido nuclear. El acento en macaguán es fonemático, como se puede ver en los siguientes ejemplos: /kénɨ/ '(yo) como' /kenɨ́/ 'uno' (número) /pajál/ 'payara' (clase de pez) /pájal/ 'paila' /néha/ 'tuyo' /nehá/ 'árbol, palo'. El tono tiende a ser más alto en las sílabas acentuadas y, en el habla rápida, inclusive la entonación es más alta por toda la oración.
new_statements.translation: The phonological word or accent group in Macaguán may consist of two to five syllables. The nuclear syllable carries a phonological accent, with slightly high pitch, as well as slight lengthening of the nuclear sound. Accent in Macaguán is phonemic, as can be seen in the following examples: /kénɨ/ '(I) eat' vs /kenɨ́/ 'one' (number); /pajál/ 'payara (a fish)' vs /pájal/ 'pan'; /néha/ 'yours' vs /nehá/ 'tree, stick'. Pitch tends to be higher on accented syllables and, in fast speech, the intonation is even higher across the whole sentence.

new_statements.rule_in_words: One accented (nuclear) syllable per phonological word of 2-5 syllables, cued by higher pitch and slight length; its position is contrastive (minimal pairs on disyllables with initial vs final accent), and the source gives no rule predicting it.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Elsewhere in ch. 2 accent interacts with allophony (aspirated stops mainly at onset of accented syllables, p. 35; palatalised /l/ at the end of accented syllables, p. 36; /a/ commonly deleted when the following syllable bears the accent, p. 39).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'palabra fonológica o grupo acentual' (2-5 syllables); examples are isolated lexical items in phonemic transcription with the accent mark on the vowel; the orthography (sec. 2.7, p. 40) writes the accent on the vowel as a suprasegmental.
new_statements.identity_note: Source calls the language 'macaguán' and the people Macaguán/Jitnu (sec. 1.1: 'Jitnu' = hit- 'gente' + -nu 'soy/somos'), spoken by ~180 people in Arauca who identify as a mix of Macaguán, Chiricoa, Cuiba and Guahibo subgroups; this is Glottolog maca1259 (Hitnu, ISO mbn) itself, not a differently named variety. No dialects are named.

sources.note: Sec. 2.1 'El grupo acentual', p. 27: the phonological word / accent group has 2-5 syllables; the nuclear syllable bears a phonological accent realised as slightly higher pitch and slight lengthening; accent is phonemic (contrastive), with three minimal pairs (/kénɨ/ 'I eat' vs /kenɨ́/ 'one'; /pajál/ vs /pájal/; /néha/ 'yours' vs /nehá/ 'tree'); no positional rule is stated. The Rosetta Project excerpt covers the whole of ch. 2 (pp. 27-40); HathiTrust holds the full book search-only.
